result.adjudicator_notes:
Perfect sweep: 9/9 recall (100%, threshold 80%), 9/9 specificity (100%, threshold 50%). No reasoning-vs-pick overrides needed — every pick token agreed with its stated reasoning.

Recall (rows 1-9): all nine agents named the C-described capability explicitly (signature / parameter / return-type lookup, unknown-identifier and type-mismatch compile errors, SKSE-plugin APIs). The description's named-vendor list (PapyrusUtil, JContainers, MCMHelper) did real work — rows 4, 5, 8 each cited the specific vendor by name as the reason C fit. Row 6 (copied-function edit) was carried by the explicit "even one copied from elsewhere in the same file" clause, which that agent quoted verbatim; that clause is load-bearing and should not be trimmed.

Specificity (rows 10-18): clean separation from the two nearest neighbours. L (papyrus-optimization) took all three cost/lag rows (10, 11, 17) with no C bleed — notably row 17, where "decompile campfire's pex" could have pulled toward a reference lookup, but the agent reasoned that decompiling is only the means and the judgment task is grading. F took the C++ native-plugin authoring row (12) despite "papyrus" in the query. G took both record-schema rows (13, 14). N correctly took the MO2 install how-to (16).

One soft spot worth noting, not a miss: row 14 ("attach this existing script to the magic effect record and fill in its properties") produced visibly unsettled reasoning — the agent cycled the whole menu, noted nothing cleanly covers VMAD script-attachment plus property filling, and landed on G by elimination. C was never a candidate in that reasoning, so specificity holds; the row exposes a menu-level gap (script-to-record wiring, which lives in the authoria-requiem pack, not the houseCARL menu) rather than a papyrus-reference defect. Re-run that row if a skill ever closes the gap.

No description change indicated for papyrus-reference.
